picks.style: late antique funeral rite, unaccompanied male voice over a low drone, slow, ceremonial, name-calling cadence
picks.why: 'The buried ashes rejoice to have their own names spoken' — the whole argument for a book of the dead, in one breath.

picks.style: latin lament, solo viol and low drone, aching baritone, very slow, bare, unresolved
picks.why: Thirty-six years a widower: the silent house, the cold bed, and every other wife a torment whether good or bad.

picks.style: pastoral dirge, single shepherd's pipe and low strings, quiet tenor, halting, tender, broken off
picks.why: The grandson named Pastor, killed by a tile from a roof — 'that tile, hurled, sought my own head'.

picks.style: late roman hymnic processional, lyre and reed pipes with light percussion, layered voices, ceremonial, festive, building
picks.why: The gods competing in song for the new Jove — 'with songs, with reeds, with thumb, with voice, with foot'.

picks.style: bacchic triumphal procession, frame drums, cymbals and double pipes, ecstatic massed voices, driving, intoxicated
picks.why: Horned Ganges led in chains while the vine that binds him sprouts leaves along his wet arms.

picks.style: late antique sea idyll, harp and soft flutes, shimmering female voice, languid, glittering, slow swell
picks.why: Triton carrying Venus through the water while Galatea plucks his side and promises a marriage in secret.

picks.style: baroque victory anthem, massed choir with organ and trumpets, majestic, thunderous, processional
picks.why: 'Up, rouze your selves, ye Nations' — the poem opens by demanding to be sung, which settles it.

picks.style: english blank-verse elegy, low strings and solo horn, sombre baritone, slow, wind-swept
picks.why: 'The Tempest saw their Strength, and sigh'd, and past them by' — the one line here worth a whole song.

picks.style: infernal recitative, dark brass and timpani, growling bass, brooding, defiant, ominous
picks.why: Satan in council: 'we fought, ye Stygian Gods, we fought' — Miltonic and genuinely stormy.

picks.style: georgian cradle song, harp and soft strings, tender soprano, gentle rocking, hopeful beneath grief
picks.why: A song to an unborn child while its father sits in prison — 'emblem of the rose unblown'. Trochaic and singable.

picks.style: english ballad lament, fiddle and guitar, plain female voice, anapaestic sway, resigned, wounded
picks.why: 'Though I die, may thy pleasure increase! Thy Mary will never repine' — a wronged wife's farewell in clean ballad stanzas.

picks.style: mourning parlour song, piano and cello, low female voice, slow, intimate, breaking
picks.why: The mother asking her dead child to visit her in dreams and bring word of when they will meet.

picks.style: comic ritual chant, croaking layered male voices over frame drum and reed pipe, insistent, looping refrain, marshy
picks.why: Brekekekex koax koax — the most famous refrain in Greek comedy, already built as a song.

picks.style: torchlight processional hymn, double aulos, cymbals and massed voices, ecstatic, quickening, radiant
picks.why: 'The meadow shines with flame; the old men's knees leap up; they shake off their griefs' — a real initiation hymn.

picks.style: greek festival dance-song, lyre and hand drums, mixed voices with call-and-response refrain, lilting, mischievous, warm
picks.why: 'Iacchus, lover of the dance, escort me' three times over, with the glimpsed girl and the all-night vigil.

picks.style: zen chant-song, shakuhachi and koto, spare male voice, slow, wandering, unadorned
picks.why: The ox-herding stanzas — the empty cries of cicadas, the deep grove, the tracks, the cord about to snap.

picks.style: zen folk verse, solo shakuhachi and light hand drum, warm quiet voice, gentle, settled, resolved
picks.why: The other half of the sequence and a complete quatrain on its own: the wild cow tamed, following like a shadow.

picks.style: greek symposium song, lyre over a low drone, wry male voice, measured, ironic, brooding
picks.why: Only candidate; 'we know those virtues, which we ne'er pursue' and the anchor dragging on loose ground both land.
